toolchain: Rust 1.99.1 release with locked dependencies; Metal 3.1 safe math

method.timing: render wall time plus PNG encoding
method.execution: sequential renderer runs; CPU and GPU benchmarks do not overlap

small_scene_followup.reason: The short 16-sphere linear case measured about 0.35 ms slower; increase work and alternate order to investigate.

validation.python_tools: syntax checks and actual benchmark, tuning, physics/PBRT runs passed

decisions: CPU and both Metal traversal modes use dedicated occlusion queries that stop at the first blocker.
CPU rejects zero-contribution direct-light samples before shadow tracing while preserving all random draws.
CPU media use prepared parent relationships and update only on dielectric transmission.
GPU early light rejection and explicit zero-absorption branching were not retained after timing trials.
Dispatch defaults were selected across the room, 64/4096-sphere hardware scenes, and the emitting cavity.
Reorganization preserves the physical estimator, RNG, HDR film, scene contract, and tested GPU layouts.
measurement_limits: Gains vary by scene and workload. The smallest 16-sphere linear case was 0.35 ms slower in the short sweep; the larger alternating followup was faster.
Driver shader caches were already warm from validation. Setup/cold-first-process data is recorded, but these are not cold-machine measurements.
Six timed GPU room runs per version are pooled for its combined median; the CPU and each dense case use three timed runs per version.
Analytical validation timings are not used for throughput claims.
Raw traces and generated EXRs remain under ignored target/optimization and target/optimization-baseline.
